title: Fiber functors for finite symmetric tensor categories in positive characteristic
main_claim: Every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p>0 has a fiber functor to Ver_{p^n}(k) for some n. This is the finite case of the BEO conjecture, and the paper includes p=2. The key new input is a proof of the Coulembier–Flake restricted-tilting conjecture: for every D, R(St_{r-1})⊗D ≅ R(T) with T tilting.
coverage:
I read every section in full: introduction, preliminaries, restricted, higher, projectivity, support, descent, and the start of consequences. I checked the following steps in detail.

(1) Restricted tilting.
- The lift of D to a degree-<q G_a-module via the coalgebra C_q≅O(E_r) is correct.
- The G-equivariant vector bundle on the punctured plane extends across the origin by reflexive hull plus Hartogs.
- The U-degree bound passes to the origin fibre because the coefficients b_j vanish.
- The identity deg L(h)=h holds.
- The BEO Lemma 3.3 induction is correct.
- In the formal comparison, Ext^1_G(T, Sym^j V*⊗T)=0 holds (Weyl filtration against good filtration), which gives the jet-by-jet equivariant lifts.
- I verified the torus-conjugation identity h u(t) h^{-1}=u(x^2 t) and the intertwining computation for f=b_h^{-1}φρ_T(h).
- Descent from K=k((x)) to k works because the intertwiner space is defined over k and k is infinite.

(2) Support and embedding selection.
- I recomputed the rank variety of Ind_H^E k and the support of St_{r-1} along u(λ_i), including the Frobenius twists.
- The Moore-matrix argument holds: B has rank r-1, its row space meets F_p^r only in 0 (via f^p−f), and so the kernel vector has F_p-independent coordinates. Raising to Frobenius powers recovers the stated equations.

(3) Minimal nonprojective rank.
- The norm-map criterion is correct.
- Internal norms of tensor products are detected by exact faithful evaluation.
- The Chouinard reduction holds, and the contradiction with CEO Lemma 4.10 is valid.
- Restrictions to proper subgroups are projective by minimality.

(4) Exactness.
- Φ(P)≠0 follows from the evaluation identity, and tensoring with Φ(P) reflects exactness.

(5) Descent.
- The congruence [Y]^{p^r} ≡ Σ(i_1…i_r)[F…F(Y)] mod p holds, using i^p≡i.
- Equality of FP dimensions forces S∈C_ex, via the categorical dimension of the invertible B, which gives a multiplicity nonzero mod p.
- The trapping argument in the finite graph is sound.
- The scalar-twisted iteration is correct.
- The Serre closure D ≃ (H/HeH)-mod is correct.
- The target is Ver_p in odd characteristic (EO Cor 9.5) and Ver_4^+ in characteristic 2 (EO Cor 9.8 / EG Thm 2.21).
- The combined functor, the final semilinearity correction, and faithfulness are all correct.

I did not independently verify these cited results:
- the Coulembier–Flake implication from the conjecture to a symmetric monoidal Θ (Thm 5.4.3, 5.2.1);
- EO Prop 6.3, Prop 7.4 and Cor 9.5/9.8;
- CEO Lemma 4.10;
- BEO Thm 4.2 and 4.34.
sibling_notes: The family 208 board had no prior entries when I checked. Companion papers may reuse two things from this one. First, the restricted-tilting theorem (Thm 3.1): its proof uses an equivariant bundle on A^2, with formal trivialization at the origin coming from Ext-vanishing between tilting modules and good-filtration modules. Second, the Moore-type selection of the embedding (Lemma 6.4).
